newsitem.title: PERU: Lima bolsa ends soft,locals cash in secondary shrs.
newsitem.headline: Lima bolsa ends soft,locals cash in secondary shrs.

text.p: Lima stocks ended weaker Wednesday principally on profit-taking from local investors in second- and third-tier stocks which had risen sharply in the previous two sessions, brokers said.
They predicted further falls on Thursday due to pending sale orders for leaders and probable further profit-taking on lower-level shares.
In Wednesday's session, the General Index fell 0.66 percent to 1,533.73 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index was off 0.38 percent to 2,062.34.
"Today the bolsa was dominated by local investors who took profits on second- and third-level shares after a substantial increase in prices," said Guillermo Siles of Argos brokerage.
Total market volume was 28 million soles ($11 million) on 2,349 trades. Overall, 42 stocks fell, 31 rose and 37 were unchanged.
Benchmark stock Telefonica del Peru gained 0.18 percent to 5.64 soles on 850,233 shares.

Among other leaders, ice-cream and confectionery firm D'Onofrio fell 3.88 percent to 1.24 soles on 304,820 shares, while Atacocha was off 2.33 percent to 0.42 sol on 704,794 shares, and brewery Cervesur lost 2.48 percent to 1.57 soles on 101,559 shares.
"At the close, most of the leaders still had sale orders. This could cause a downward trend on Thursday," said Alex Balarin of Macrovalores brokerage.
Brokers said, however, that the market's medium-term prospects were still positive due to the economy's solid first half performance and good second half expectations.
